acoustic.dominant_character: The recording is dominated by the continuous, high-frequency crackling of snapping shrimp, with a low-frequency vessel passage audible in the latter half.
acoustic.calibration_caveat: Absolute sound pressure level cannot be derived without the deployment calibration constant, which is not present in this file.

imagery.spatial_summary: Samples are plotted along the Florida coastline, with clusters of 'not present' (grey), 'very low' (white), and 'low' (yellow) concentrations observed near Jacksonville on the east coast, around the Tampa Bay and Clearwater areas on the west coast, and along the Panhandle.
imagery.determinability_caveat: A shellfish harvesting closure decision cannot be made from this image alone because it is a broad-scale public informational map that lacks the precise, localized cell counts and regulatory testing data required by authorities to enforce closures.

regulatory.cell_count_explanation: The document does not establish a specific numeric cell-count threshold for Karenia brevis or NSP. It states that 'either cell counts of the toxin producing organism in the water column or biotoxin meat concentrations may be used by the Authority as the criteria for not allowing the harvest of shellstock' only '[f]or any marine biotoxin for which criteria have not been established under this Ordinance' (page 70). Since NSP criteria are established, this clause does not apply. Furthermore, the guidance section notes that '[c]ell counts, as measured per liter of water, are often used to trigger additional testing of shellfish in biotoxin monitoring programs' but that '[t]hese cell count criteria can only be established with a robust dataset' (page 359).

citations.provision_reference: Section II Model Ordinance Chapter IV @ .04 C. (1) (b)

citations.verbatim_quote: A growing area, or portion(s) thereof, shall be placed in the closed status for the taking of shellstock when the Authority determines that the number of toxin-forming organisms in the growing waters and/or the level of biotoxin present in shellfish meats is sufficient to cause a health risk.
citations.provision_reference: Section II Model Ordinance Chapter IV @ .04 C. (1)

regulatory.caveats: The document does not contain any Florida-specific requirements or any numeric cell-count threshold (such as 5,000 cells per liter) for Karenia brevis or NSP closures.

assessment.headline: The public map reads 'low', every value of which is at or above Florida's 5,000 cells/L closure trigger.
assessment.band_explanation: The whole 'low' band starts at 10,000 cells/L, at or above the 5,000 cells/L closure trigger. Every sample in this category is over the trigger.
assessment.reconciliation: Cell counts trigger TESTING. Toxin in meat triggers CLOSURE. Florida's 5,000 cells/L figure is a state operational trigger, not a federal action level: it appears nowhere in the NSSP Guide. The federal criterion is 20 MU/100 grams (0.8 mg brevetoxin-2 equivalents/kg), measured in shellfish meats.
caveats: A category on a public map is not a measurement. No cells-per-liter figure is derived from map color anywhere in this system.

write_advisory.advisory:
ADVISORY

The public map reads 'low', every value of which is at or above Florida's 5,000 cells/L closure trigger.

Federal criterion: 20 MU/100 grams (0.8 mg brevetoxin-2 equivalents/kg)

Cell counts trigger TESTING. Toxin in meat triggers CLOSURE. Florida's 5,000 cells/L figure is a state operational trigger, not a federal action level: it appears nowhere in the NSSP Guide. The federal criterion is 20 MU/100 grams (0.8 mg brevetoxin-2 equivalents/kg), measured in shellfish meats.

This advisory is generated from archived public data for demonstration. It is not an official determination. Harvesting area status is set by the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Division of Aquaculture.
